nodes.label: Architecture: Form, Space, & Order
nodes.description: A comprehensive primer on the ways form and space are interrelated and organized in the shaping of the architectural environment.

nodes.label: Primary Elements
nodes.description: The foundational geometric entities that generate form, starting from the point to one-dimensional, two-dimensional, and three-dimensional elements.

nodes.label: Point
nodes.description: Marks a position in space. Conceptually has no length, width, or depth; static, centralized, and directionless.

nodes.label: Line
nodes.description: A point extended in space, possessing length, direction, and position.

nodes.label: Plane
nodes.description: A line extended in a direction other than its intrinsic direction, possessing length, width, shape, surface, orientation, and position.

nodes.label: Volume
nodes.description: A plane extended in a direction other than its intrinsic direction, possessing length, width, depth, form and space.

nodes.label: Form
nodes.description: The formal structure of a work, the manner of arranging elements to produce a coherent image.

nodes.label: Shape
nodes.description: The characteristic outline or surface configuration of a particular form.

nodes.label: Size
nodes.description: The physical dimensions of length, width, and depth of a form.

nodes.label: Color
nodes.description: The attribute that most clearly distinguishes a form from its environment.

nodes.label: Texture
nodes.description: The visual and tactile quality given to a surface.

nodes.label: Form and Space
nodes.description: The symbiotic relationship where forms define and enclose spaces.

nodes.label: Horizontal Elements Defining Space
nodes.description: Base planes, elevated base planes, depressed base planes, and overhead planes.

nodes.label: Vertical Elements Defining Space
nodes.description: Vertical linear elements, single vertical planes, L-shaped planes, parallel planes, U-shaped planes, and four planes (enclosure).

nodes.label: Organization
nodes.description: The spatial relationships and configurations of spaces within a building.

nodes.label: Centralized Organization
nodes.description: A central, dominant space about which a number of secondary spaces are grouped.

nodes.label: Linear Organization
nodes.description: A linear sequence of repetitive spaces.

nodes.label: Radial Organization
nodes.description: A central space from which linear organizations of space extend in a radial manner.

nodes.label: Clustered Organization
nodes.description: Spaces grouped by proximity or the sharing of a common visual trait or relationship.

nodes.label: Grid Organization
nodes.description: Spaces organized within the field of a structural grid or another three-dimensional framework.

nodes.label: Circulation
nodes.description: The movement through space, elements including approach, entrance, configuration of the path, path-space relationships, and form of the circulation space.

nodes.label: Proportion and Scale
nodes.description: Systems that govern the visual and structural scale of forms, including the Golden Section, Modulor, and anthropometry.

nodes.label: Principles
nodes.description: Ordering principles that orchestrate form and space into a unified whole.

nodes.label: Axis
nodes.description: A line established by two points in space, about which forms and spaces can be arranged in a symmetrical or balanced manner.

nodes.label: Symmetry
nodes.description: The balanced distribution and arrangement of equivalent forms and spaces on opposite sides of a dividing line or plane.

nodes.label: Hierarchy
nodes.description: The articulation of the importance or significance of a form or space by its size, shape, or placement relative to the other forms and spaces.

nodes.label: Rhythm
nodes.description: A unifying movement characterized by a patterned repetition or alternation of formal elements or motifs.

nodes.label: Datum
nodes.description: A line, plane, or volume that, by its continuity and regularity, serves to gather, measure, and organize a pattern of forms and spaces.

nodes.label: Transformation
nodes.description: The principle that an architectural concept, structure, or organization can be altered through a series of discrete manipulations in response to a specific context.
